We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (three outcomes). We need to choose one that can be further processed with next template 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We attempted applying 1914389 to one of the outcomes: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". That gave two products: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". The template likely splits a protecting group? Not sure.

We need to continue chain: after 1914389, we apply 1914390 to each product? The order is fixed, so each step must be a reaction using that template, producing precursors for next step.

Thus we need a linear chain of 5 reactions: target -> after 29646 -> after 1914389 -> after 1914390 -> after 149040 -> after 1914391 -> final precursors (starting materials). We need to ensure each application yields at least one product that can be further processed.

We have applied 1914390 to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" and got "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". Good.

Now apply 149040 to that product. It returned empty, meaning template not applicable. Maybe we need to choose different branch.

Alternative: after 1914389, we could take the other product "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". Apply 1914390 to that? It gave empty earlier. So not.

Maybe we need to apply 1914390 to the first product "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" gave product we tried. Could there be alternative outcome from 1914390? It gave only one product.

Maybe we need to apply 149040 to a different precursor earlier. Perhaps after 1914389 we could choose a different outcome from 29646? The 29646 gave three possible outcomes: each with a silyl protecting group maybe. Let's view them: result from 29646: 
1) 'C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C'
2) 'C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO'
3) 'C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO'

We need to pick one that after 1914389 yields a product that can go through 1914390 etc.

We tried first one (with silyl on side chain) and got same as earlier. That gave product after 1914389: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" (plus other). That seems promising.

Now need to apply 1914390 to that product gave "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". This product maybe can undergo 149040 (which seems to be a deprotection of silyl? Actually 149040 is a silicon removal? The template shows Si to O conversion. It converts a Si-O bond to C-O? The retro template: [C:2]-[Si...]...>>... So it removes silyl protecting group. Our current product does not have Si. So 149040 not applicable.

Thus maybe we need to apply 149040 earlier, before 1914390? But order is fixed.

Maybe the correct chain is: after 1914389 we get a silyl-protected intermediate that later 1914390 removes something else, then 149040 removes silyl. Let's examine the product from 1914389: we got two products, one is silyl-protected (the first) and the other is a phosphonate? Actually "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC" is a phosphonate with silyl? No.

The first product "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" has no Si. So not.

Maybe we need to apply 1914389 to a different outcome from 29646 that retains Si. Let's try applying 1914389 to the second outcome: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO".
